summary: Aroostook County, ME: state station from 1909, 60-ft steel tower from 1914, closed 1973, removed 1995-2005 per FFLOS; no description of the site today found.

facts.design: 60-foot steel tower erected 1914, replacing a platform station in a spruce tree
facts.status_note: Closed in 1973 and removed between 1995 and 2005 per the FFLOS entry; no description of the site today found

events.note: State station built on the mountain in 1909. The 1914 report calls it a platform in a spruce tree; a Maine Memory record calls it a wood tower
New 60-foot steel tower erected after the platform became unsafe. A Maine Memory slideshow caption says 63 feet
Telephone line of about 22 miles built from Depot Mountain to English Lake
Clyde Fox of St. Pamphile, Quebec, was the watchman; Grover Bradford of Sebec was chief warden
Steel tower repainted and reported to be in good condition
Maine Memory slideshow says the tower, at 1,300 feet, closed in 1973; another Maine Memory record (19115) gives the new tower an elevation of 1,300 feet
FFLOS says removed between 1995 and 2005; 1995 is the start of that range, not a confirmed date
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.quote: The tower was removed between 1995 and 2005.
Aroostook County, Maine

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Maine Memory record and the Forest Lookouts page give 60 feet for the 1914 tower; a Maine Memory slideshow caption gives 63 feet. The record and the register figure of 60 feet are used here, and the 63-foot figure is noted as a disagreement.
A 1914 state report, quoted by the Forest Lookouts page, calls the 1909 station a platform in a spruce tree. A Maine Memory record calls it a wood tower. The story reports both descriptions.

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site today, and no access information was found, so access and visit keys are omitted. Township disagrees across sources: Forest Lookouts quotes 'Twp. No. 18 R. 16'; the Maine Memory record keywords say T14 R16 WELS; a DigitalMaine map title seen only in a search snippet says Township 11 Range 16. Not used in the story. Maine Memory record 19115 has a photo, but no image URL was retrieved, so no photo entry.
